scope the partner-sum distribution to bound antisymmetric tensors

impl.criterion: Rule (ii). SlotContraction::find_contraction's Add-partner arm admits a partner sum only if `binds_antisymmetric` holds: a metric (when metrics are enabled) or a rank-one vector (when rank_one) of the source sum must bind a slot of an antisymmetric tensor in some linear term of the partner sum. That slot must be permitted by `representations` and must not be a colour slot (ColorFundamental, ColorAdjoint or ColorSextet). Colour slots, such as those of f, are left to the colour algebra. In every other case both sums stay factorized, as before #151. Single tensor partners, expand=false and the planner are unchanged.
impl.classification:
The 17 remaining #151 copies in finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed are the same in both coupling orders. In every one, the copied slot is a Lorentz slot mink(dim,i) carried by the metric g and by momenta Q in the partner sum. No colour or spinor slot is copied, no epsilon is involved, and f never carries the copied slot. I confirmed each decline reason with a planner probe: replacing the named construct in the dumped domain by a plain tensor makes the planner return Complete.
(a) 5 copies: products of two four-gluon 3x3 vertex sums. The planner declines because gluon-propagator colour metrics g(coad,coad) bind ports of f. The literal fallback absorbs those colour metrics first and then copies a vertex sum through the other via a Lorentz slot. In 4 of them the slot sits on metrics; in 1 it sits on metrics and momenta (vector source).
(b1) 8 copies: 6x6 and 6x7 products. The planner declines because of colour trace(coad(8),sym(f(..,in,out),..)) notation in a 7-term colour sum that is connected by Lorentz slots. One copy turns a 4.8 KB product into a 75 KB replacement.
(b2) 4 copies: 2x5 products with rank_one=false. The planner declines because of colour chain(coad,coad,f(..,in,out),..) notation. The previous agent's 'Q^2 under rank_one=false' reason was not confirmed: the probe shows the chain is the cause, in both rank_one modes.
Across all 81 test_renormalization tests, #151 makes 351 copies (default registration) and 297 (model order). Almost all are mink slots on g/Q. A few others are colour-metric sums whose partner carries the slot on f, or on chain/gamma bodies. Rule (i) admits only the f cases: 2 copies by default and 8 with model order, in d45-d47, d69-d71, d74 and d75. There the source is a counterterm sum whose every term carries g(coad(a),coad(b)), and the partner is f*f*cas + f*f*cas + trace(..).
#151's motivating products are all admitted by the chosen rule:
- Its first test, `(x*p(a)+y*q(a))*(z*T(a)+epsilon(a,b,c,d))` and the metric-sum variant: Lorentz slot, carried by epsilon in one term; the source binds epsilon's port.
- Its second test: the slot is carried by vector p0 in one partner term and by epsilon in the other; the vector source binds epsilon.
- The NinjaRS e+ e- -> Z a product `c*(Σ dot·P_i(μ))*(Σ P_j(μ) ε(K,P_j,..) + ε(μ,P_j,..))`: μ=mink(4,hedge(5,1)) is carried by P_j or by epsilon. The planner declines because the source vectors bind epsilon's μ.

impl.pr_title: idenso: contract around symmetric spectators and copy partner sums only into bound antisymmetric tensors
impl.pr_body:
## Summary

`finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed` spent most of its contraction time copying sums. The component planner declined every product that contained a symmetric, antisymmetric or cyclic head. Take a four-gluon vertex such as

```
f(a1,a2,e)*f(a3,a4,e)*(g(m1,m3)*g(m2,m4) - g(m1,m4)*g(m2,m3)) + (2 more terms)
```

times another vertex sum that shares the Lorentz slots `m1, m4`. The planner declined it because of `f`, although `f` carries none of the contracted slots. The literal fallback then applied #151's partner-sum rule and contracted it as 3 × 3 copies. The same rule also fired on products the planner declines for unrelated colour notation. For example, a 7-term colour-`trace` sum times a 6-term three-gluon sum turned a 4.8 KB product into a 75 KB replacement. With coupling symbols registered in model order, the test took 483–525 s, against 95–128 s before #151.

This PR has two commits:

1. The component planner contracts around symmetric spectators.
2. #151's partner-sum copies are limited to the case they were added for: a metric or vector binding a slot of an antisymmetric tensor such as `epsilon`.

The test now takes 56–58 s (0.58–0.59 × pristine `feynkit` 58814885), and 66–67 s with model-order registration.

### Cause

- `ComponentSum` (`slot_contraction/components.rs`) treated every head with a permutation symmetry as opaque. So `f` beside contracted Lorentz slots sent the whole component to the literal fallback in `SlotContraction::find_contraction`.
- Since #151, that fallback passes a source sum through a partner sum whenever the planner declines, whatever the reason. Even with commit 1, `finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed` still made 17 such copies in each coupling order. Every one copies a Lorentz slot carried by metrics and momenta. The products fall into three groups:
  - 5 four-gluon 3×3 products, declined because gluon-propagator colour metrics `g(coad,coad)` bind `f`
  - 8 products declined because of colour `trace(coad,sym(f(..,in,out),..))` notation
  - 4 products declined because of colour `chain` notation

  Replacing the named construct by a plain tensor makes the planner contract each of them.

### Change

- **Planner spectators** (`contract around symmetric spectator tensors in the component planner`):
  - A head whose only non-plain attributes are permutation symmetries enters as `TensorSource::Spectator`.
  - Its explicit ports join the incidence graph, so degree and dummy checks still apply, but no contraction may bind them. `bind()` declines the component when a vector, a metric relabelling or an earlier selected factor would change a written argument.
  - Spectators are emitted with their written arguments.
- **Scoped partner-sum arm** (`scope the partner-sum distribution to bound antisymmetric tensors`):
  - `find_contraction` now admits a partner *sum* only if `binds_antisymmetric` holds: a metric or vector of the source sum binds a non-colour slot of an antisymmetric tensor in some term of the partner sum. That is exactly the binding the planner declines for `epsilon`.
  - Colour slots, such as those of `f`, are left to the colour algebra.
  - Otherwise both sums stay factorized, as before #151.

Choice of rule: I compared three rules, all of which keep #151's tests and remove the 17 copies in the developed test:
- (i) any antisymmetric tensor carries the bound slot
- (ii) the same, restricted to non-colour slots (chosen)
- (iii) only `epsilon` carries it

Across all 81 `test_renormalization` tests, (i) still copies colour sums in d45–d47, d69–d71, d74 and d75: 2 products with default coupling registration and 8 with model-order registration. In those products every term of a counterterm sum carries `g(coad(a),coad(b))`, and the partner sum is `f*f*cas + f*f*cas + trace(..)`. The copy costs +37 % instructions (callgrind) and +32 % size, and the contraction still ends Deferred. (ii) and (iii) make no copies there, the same as with the arm off. (ii) is preferred over (iii) because it does not single out one symbol: `charge_conjugation` or a user-defined antisymmetric tensor still qualifies.

### What does not change

- #151's two tests and its example: `(a*p1(i)+b*p2(i))*(c*p0(i)+d*epsilon(i,p0,e2,e3))` still contracts.
- Single tensor partners, metric-first substitution, `expand = false`, and the refusal when some source term has no port.
- The planner still declines heads with normalization callbacks, evaluation, or linear or flat attributes; chain and trace notation; and untagged projectors.
- Scalar spectators, factored sums, powers and foreign tensors keep their existing treatment.

### Context

- #151 (Valentin Hirschi) added the partner-sum copies for NinjaRS γ5 numerators in `e+ e- -> Z a`:

  ```
  c*(Σ dot·P_i(μ))*(Σ … P_j(μ) ε(K,P_j,ϵ̄2,ϵ̄3) + … ε(μ,P_j,ϵ̄2,ϵ̄3))
  ```

  Some partner terms carry μ on a vector and others on `epsilon`. The source vectors bind epsilon's μ, so commit 2 still admits the product. The new unit test covers this shape.
- Model-order registration is the held change "register coupling symbols and overall-factor heads in a fixed order". Here it was emulated by an env-gated scratch patch that registers the UFO couplings in model order. It is not part of this PR.
- `slow::finite_part_photon_3loop_no_ghost` fails on pristine 58814885 with the same message as on this branch: "d22 differs from its RQFT reference", with leftover `MD^2` terms. It fails with or without either commit, and also with #151's arm off. On this branch it fails after 209 s instead of 1406 s.

## Tests and measurements

- New `slot_contraction::tests::partner_sums_are_copied_only_into_bound_antisymmetric_tensors` tests the literal contractor.
  - It copies the `e+ e- -> Z a` shape (vector in one term, `epsilon` in the other) and a generic antisymmetric Lorentz tensor.
  - It leaves unchanged: plain tensor partners; gluon-vertex-like sums beside `f` that share Lorentz slots on metrics and momenta only; an `epsilon` whose slots no source binds; and a colour-metric sum binding `f`.
  - It fails with #151's unscoped arm, and its colour case fails under rule (i).
- `components::tests::symmetric_spectator_contractions_match_the_literal_rewrite` (from commit 1):
  - Its reference is now the literal rewrite of the expanded product, because the fallback no longer copies sums.
  - It also asserts that for `g(coad(a1),coad(b1))*vertex*vertex` the fallback relabels one vertex and keeps both sums, while the typed contraction still equals the expanded reference.
  - It asserts that a Lorentz-connected sum with colour `trace` notation is declined and stays as written.
- Workspace checks, in `nix develop` (rustc 1.98.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.143, licensed Symbolica):
  - `cargo nextest run -p idenso --lib --cargo-profile ci-optim --profile ci_gammaloop`: 1056 passed, 24 skipped.
  - `cargo nextest run -p spenso -p feynkit-generator -p feynkit-graph --lib --cargo-profile ci-optim --profile ci_gammaloop`: 628 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p idenso --all-targets --no-deps --locked --profile ci-optim -- --deny warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `test_renormalization` (ci-optim), built from this branch plus the env-gated model-order patch:
  - All 70 `finite_part_ghost_*` tests pass in both coupling orders, one process per test.
  - The whole binary in one process with model-order registration: 80 passed, 1 failed (`slow::finite_part_photon_3loop_no_ghost`, see Context).
- Partner-sum copies, default / model-order registration:

  | | developed | all 81 tests |
  |---|---|---|
  | commit 1 + #151 arm | 17 / 17 | 351 / 297 |
  | rule (i) | 0 / 0 | 2 / 8 |
  | rule (ii), this PR | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
  | rule (iii) | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
  | arm off | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

- `finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed` wall clock over 3 rounds, as a ratio to pristine 58814885 (default registration) run concurrently in the same round:

  | | default | model order |
  |---|---|---|
  | this PR (quiet host; pristine 96.6–98.0 s) | 0.58–0.59 (55.7–58.1 s) | 0.68 (65.7–66.8 s) |
  | rule (i) | 0.56–0.70 | 0.64–0.70 |
  | rule (ii) | 0.56–0.71 | 0.65–0.71 |
  | rule (iii) | 0.57–0.72 | 0.68–0.85 |
  | arm off | 0.56–0.72 | 0.67–0.69 |
  | commit 1 + #151 arm | 0.98–1.04 | 0.87–0.96 |
  | upstream planner + #151 arm | 0.95–1.26 | 4.42–4.78 (483–525 s) |

  - The rule rows come from scratch builds that select the rule through an environment variable, at host load 150–230.
  - For d42, d43, d44 and the colour-copy tests (d45–d47, d69–d71, d74, d75), the rules agree within round-to-round noise. With model-order registration, d44 runs 3–21 % slower than pristine under every variant, the #151 arm included.
- Callgrind on the typed contraction of declined developed-test products, #151 arm → this PR:
  - four-gluon domain: 34.0 M → 30.4 M Ir, same Complete result
  - trace domain: 113.0 M → 30.8 M Ir, output 38.4 KB → 2.9 KB
  - chain domain: 14.1 M → 10.2 M Ir

`nix-ci.nix` keeps `enable = false` during review.

CI artifacts were not uploaded.

open_issues: The chosen rule (ii) is not your example (i). That is your call. Evidence: (i) still copies colour-metric sums through f in d45-d47, d69-d71, d74 and d75 (2 copies with default registration, 8 with model order). On that product the copy costs +37% instructions and +32% size, and the contraction stays Deferred. Wall clock does not separate (i) from (ii). Switching to (i) means removing the COLOR_REPRESENTATIONS filter in binds_antisymmetric and moving the colour case of the new test from the unchanged list to the copied list.

slow::finite_part_photon_3loop_no_ghost fails on pristine feynkit 58814885 ('d22 differs from its RQFT reference', leftover MD^2 terms). It fails the same way with either commit, with the #151 arm off, and on this branch. It is pre-existing and was not investigated.

AGENTS.md asks for maintainer confirmation before adding helpers. This change adds the private helpers SlotContraction::binds_antisymmetric and visit_linear (I found no existing walker over linear structure) and a COLOR_REPRESENTATIONS list. Equivalent colour-representation lists already exist inline in color/simplify.rs and tensor/simplification.rs; I left those as they are.
Model-order registration was measured with the previous agent's env-gated scratch patch to feynkit-model, not with the held change wsmxownt itself.
The previous agent's 'Q(k,mink(dim,i))^2 under rank_one=false' decline reason was not confirmed. The planner probe attributes those 4 copies to colour chain notation.
The first change's description still reads 'literal fallback with #151's rule'. It is accurate for that commit and was left unchanged.
Nothing was pushed and no PR was opened. CI artifacts were not uploaded, just ci-checks-and-upload was not run, and nix-ci.nix keeps enable = false.

Kept for review: /tmp/codex-combined-s2/idenso-planner-opaque-spectators. It holds s3/ (scripts, logs, dumps, probe, callgrind), bins/ (pristine, v4 rule-variant and final test binaries, scratch_contract-v4; about 363 MB), tree/ (final code plus the env-gated model-order patch) and NOTES.txt (an appended section on this step). I removed my unused idenso-lib-v4 binary.

final.pr_title: idenso: contract around symmetric spectators and copy partner sums only into bound antisymmetric tensors
final.pr_body:
## Summary

`finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed` spent most of its contraction time copying sums. The component planner declined every product that contained a symmetric, antisymmetric or cyclic head. Take a four-gluon vertex such as

```
f(a1,a2,e)*f(a3,a4,e)*(g(m1,m3)*g(m2,m4) - g(m1,m4)*g(m2,m3)) + (2 more terms)
```

times another vertex sum that shares the Lorentz slots `m1, m4`. The planner declined it because of `f`, although `f` carries none of the contracted slots. The literal fallback then applied #151's partner-sum rule and contracted it as 3 × 3 copies. The same rule also fired on products the planner declines for unrelated colour notation. For example, a 7-term colour-`trace` sum times a 6-term three-gluon sum turned a 4.8 KB product into a 75 KB replacement. With coupling symbols registered in model order, the test took 483–525 s, against 95–128 s before #151.

This PR has two commits:

1. The component planner contracts around symmetric spectators.
2. #151's partner-sum copies are limited to the case they were added for: a metric or vector binding a slot of an antisymmetric tensor such as `epsilon`.

The test now takes 56–58 s (0.58–0.59 × pristine `feynkit` 58814885), and 66–67 s with model-order registration.

### Cause

- `ComponentSum` (`slot_contraction/components.rs`) treated every head with a permutation symmetry as opaque. So `f` beside contracted Lorentz slots sent the whole component to the literal fallback in `SlotContraction::find_contraction`.
- Since #151, that fallback passes a source sum through a partner sum whenever the planner declines, whatever the reason. Even with commit 1, `finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed` still made 17 such copies in each coupling order. Every one copies a Lorentz slot carried by metrics and momenta. The products fall into three groups:
  - 5 four-gluon 3×3 products, declined because gluon-propagator colour metrics `g(coad,coad)` bind `f`
  - 8 products declined because of colour `trace(coad,sym(f(..,in,out),..))` notation
  - 4 products declined because of colour `chain` notation

  Replacing the named construct by a plain tensor makes the planner contract each of them.

### Change

- **Planner spectators** (`contract around symmetric spectator tensors in the component planner`):
  - A head whose only non-plain attributes are permutation symmetries enters as `TensorSource::Spectator`.
  - Its explicit ports join the incidence graph, so degree and dummy checks still apply, but no contraction may bind them. `bind()` declines the component when a vector, a metric relabelling or an earlier selected factor would change a written argument.
  - Spectators are emitted with their written arguments.
- **Scoped partner-sum arm** (`scope the partner-sum distribution to bound antisymmetric tensors`):
  - `find_contraction` now admits a partner *sum* only if `binds_antisymmetric` holds: a metric or vector of the source sum binds a non-colour slot of an antisymmetric tensor in some term of the partner sum. That is exactly the binding the planner declines for `epsilon`.
  - Colour slots, such as those of `f`, are left to the colour algebra.
  - Otherwise both sums stay factorized, as before #151.

Choice of rule: I compared three rules, all of which keep #151's tests and remove the 17 copies in the developed test:
- (i) any antisymmetric tensor carries the bound slot
- (ii) the same, restricted to non-colour slots (chosen)
- (iii) only `epsilon` carries it

Across all 81 `test_renormalization` tests, (i) still copies colour sums in d45–d47, d69–d71, d74 and d75: 2 products with default coupling registration and 8 with model-order registration. In those products every term of a counterterm sum carries `g(coad(a),coad(b))`, and the partner sum is `f*f*cas + f*f*cas + trace(..)`. The copy costs +37 % instructions (callgrind) and +32 % size, and the contraction still ends Deferred. (ii) and (iii) make no copies there, the same as with the arm off. (ii) is preferred over (iii) because it does not single out one symbol: `charge_conjugation` or a user-defined antisymmetric tensor still qualifies.

### What does not change

- #151's two tests and its example: `(a*p1(i)+b*p2(i))*(c*p0(i)+d*epsilon(i,p0,e2,e3))` still contracts.
- Single tensor partners, metric-first substitution, `expand = false`, and the refusal when some source term has no port.
- The planner still declines heads with normalization callbacks, evaluation, or linear or flat attributes; chain and trace notation; and untagged projectors.
- Scalar spectators, factored sums, powers and foreign tensors keep their existing treatment.

### Context

- #151 (Valentin Hirschi) added the partner-sum copies for NinjaRS γ5 numerators in `e+ e- -> Z a`:

  ```
  c*(Σ dot·P_i(μ))*(Σ … P_j(μ) ε(K,P_j,ϵ̄2,ϵ̄3) + … ε(μ,P_j,ϵ̄2,ϵ̄3))
  ```

  Some partner terms carry μ on a vector and others on `epsilon`. The source vectors bind epsilon's μ, so commit 2 still admits the product. The new unit test covers this shape.
- Model-order registration is the held change "register coupling symbols and overall-factor heads in a fixed order". Here it was emulated by an env-gated scratch patch that registers the UFO couplings in model order. It is not part of this PR.
- `slow::finite_part_photon_3loop_no_ghost` fails on pristine 58814885 with the same message as on this branch: "d22 differs from its RQFT reference", with leftover `MD^2` terms. It fails with or without either commit, and also with #151's arm off. On this branch it fails after 209 s instead of 1406 s.

## Tests and measurements

- New `slot_contraction::tests::partner_sums_are_copied_only_into_bound_antisymmetric_tensors` tests the literal contractor.
  - It copies the `e+ e- -> Z a` shape (vector in one term, `epsilon` in the other) and a generic antisymmetric Lorentz tensor.
  - It leaves unchanged: plain tensor partners; gluon-vertex-like sums beside `f` that share Lorentz slots on metrics and momenta only; an `epsilon` whose slots no source binds; and a colour-metric sum binding `f`.
  - It fails with #151's unscoped arm, and its colour case fails under rule (i).
- `components::tests::symmetric_spectator_contractions_match_the_literal_rewrite` (from commit 1):
  - Its reference is now the literal rewrite of the expanded product, because the fallback no longer copies sums.
  - It also asserts that for `g(coad(a1),coad(b1))*vertex*vertex` the fallback relabels one vertex and keeps both sums, while the typed contraction still equals the expanded reference.
  - It asserts that a Lorentz-connected sum with colour `trace` notation is declined and stays as written.
- Workspace checks, in `nix develop` (rustc 1.98.1, cargo-nextest 0.9.143, licensed Symbolica):
  - `cargo nextest run -p idenso --lib --cargo-profile ci-optim --profile ci_gammaloop`: 1056 passed, 24 skipped.
  - `cargo nextest run -p spenso -p feynkit-generator -p feynkit-graph --lib --cargo-profile ci-optim --profile ci_gammaloop`: 628 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p idenso --all-targets --no-deps --locked --profile ci-optim -- --deny warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `test_renormalization` (ci-optim), built from this branch plus the env-gated model-order patch:
  - All 70 `finite_part_ghost_*` tests pass in both coupling orders, one process per test.
  - The whole binary in one process with model-order registration: 80 passed, 1 failed (`slow::finite_part_photon_3loop_no_ghost`, see Context).
- Partner-sum copies, default / model-order registration:

  | | developed | all 81 tests |
  |---|---|---|
  | commit 1 + #151 arm | 17 / 17 | 351 / 297 |
  | rule (i) | 0 / 0 | 2 / 8 |
  | rule (ii), this PR | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
  | rule (iii) | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
  | arm off | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

- `finite_part_ghost_3loop_developed` wall clock over 3 rounds, as a ratio to pristine 58814885 (default registration) run concurrently in the same round:

  | | default | model order |
  |---|---|---|
  | this PR (quiet host; pristine 96.6–98.0 s) | 0.58–0.59 (55.7–58.1 s) | 0.68 (65.7–66.8 s) |
  | rule (i) | 0.56–0.70 | 0.64–0.70 |
  | rule (ii) | 0.56–0.71 | 0.65–0.71 |
  | rule (iii) | 0.57–0.72 | 0.68–0.85 |
  | arm off | 0.56–0.72 | 0.67–0.69 |
  | commit 1 + #151 arm | 0.98–1.04 | 0.87–0.96 |
  | upstream planner + #151 arm | 0.95–1.26 | 4.42–4.78 (483–525 s) |

  - The rule rows come from scratch builds that select the rule through an environment variable, at host load 150–230.
  - For d42, d43, d44 and the colour-copy tests (d45–d47, d69–d71, d74, d75), the rules agree within round-to-round noise. With model-order registration, d44 runs 3–21 % slower than pristine under every variant, the #151 arm included.
- Callgrind on the typed contraction of declined developed-test products, #151 arm → this PR:
  - four-gluon domain: 34.0 M → 30.4 M Ir, same Complete result
  - trace domain: 113.0 M → 30.8 M Ir, output 38.4 KB → 2.9 KB
  - chain domain: 14.1 M → 10.2 M Ir
